messages.content:
Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

Now perform the same with the following input
input: {
    "question": "user: Can you summarize the process of entity extraction?\nassistant: Entity extraction is the process of identifying and categorizing key items such as people, places, and organizations within a given text. IBM Cloud's Discovery tool utilizes advanced statistical algorithms and natural language processing technology to perform this task. By applying these techniques, the tool enhances the semantic understanding of the content, allowing for a better grasp of the subject and context of the analyzed text. It also offers support for multilingual analysis and context-sensitive disambiguation. Furthermore, you can create and integrate a custom entity model using IBM Watson Knowledge Studio for more precise entity recognition.\nuser: What is an entity extractor?\nassistant: An entity extractor is a machine learning model that identifies and tags terms that are important for your business needs or use case. When you create an entity extractor, you determine the content and scope of the information to be found and extracted. This feature is offered by IBM Watson Knowledge Studio and is designed to recognize and categorize key items, such as people, places, and organizations, within a given text. It utilizes advanced statistical algorithms and natural language processing technology to accomplish this task. \nThe tool also supports multilingual analysis and context-sensitive disambiguation. Furthermore, you have the option to create and integrate a custom entity model for more accurate entity recognition. \nIt is a component of the advanced rules feature in IBM Watson Knowledge Studio, which allows for greater customization potential in text analysis. The visual advanced rules editor includes sample extractors, such as Finance Actions extractors and Parts of Speech, which can be edited and combined to develop custom advanced rules models. These models can be used to analyze documents directly in the editor or exported for use with other services, such as Natural Language Understanding.\nuser: How can I make an extractor available to all projects?\nassistant: To make an extractor available to all projects, click Save Extractor on the toolbar for the canvas. Custom extractors are saved on the Extractors tab in the tauser folder by default. As a best practice, save modified versions of a provided extractor in the same folder as the provided extractor.\nuser: Adding an extractor to the canvas\nassistant: To add an extractor to the canvas, follow these steps:\n1. Click the Extractors tab in the Projects and Extractors pane.\n2. Drag and drop the desired extractor from the pane onto the canvas.\nIf you want to add multiple instances of the same extractor, ensure you rename each instance when dragging it to the canvas to prevent them from being treated as a single extractor. If you have renamed two or more instances, you can right-click and select Unlink to create a copy.\nuser: Is any kind of expertise required to use this tool?\nassistant: I do not have that information. \nuser: It's okay, but it would be helpful to have more information.\nassistant: Yes, indeed! \nuser: Is it possible to create extractors with linguistic patterns?\nassistant: Yes. To extract text from documents in non-English languages, you can either modify existing extractors or create new ones based on linguistic patterns. If your target terms follow a specific pattern, you can design a sequence pattern for extraction.\nYou can utilize the workspace to create extractors that can work with any language, including Spanish and French, using tokens defined by whitespace and punctuation. Building a new extractor involves using natural language processing (NLP) concepts such as tokenization and part-of-speech tagging, and it requires the development of an extractor using the Annotation Query Language (AQL). \nFor information on the languages that are supported for tokenization and part-of-speech analysis, please refer to the section on Multilingual Support for Text Analytics. \nuser: How do the semantics of an extract pattern work?\nassistant: The semantics of an extract pattern involve defining a specific pattern to match in the text and specifying what should be returned by the extractor. This pattern specification consists of multiple elements, which can be columns from previously defined views, fixed strings, or regular expressions. You have the option to make these elements optional and allow them to repeat, as well as to define gaps between them.\nIn simpler terms, an extract pattern is a way to create a specific search query or rule for extracting relevant information from text. The pattern specification details the structure and components of the information you wish to extract, while the return clause indicates how the extracted information should be processed.\nFor instance, if you want to extract all the names of people and their corresponding ages from a text, you could define an extract pattern that identifies sequences of words that match a person's name (e.g., a sequence of words starting with a capital letter and containing only letters), followed by the word \"is\" or \"are,\" and then a number signifying the person's age. The pattern specification would describe the structure of this sequence, and the return clause would specify that the extracted information should be returned as a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a name and an age.\nuser: What is an identifier?",
    "answer": "标识符是用于唯一标识一个实体的名称。它分为未加引号的标识符和反引号标识符。未加引号的标识符至少包含一个字符，可使用数字、字母和下划线；反引号标识符由重音符号（`）括起，可以包含任意字符。"
}
Output:

statements: 标识符是用于唯一标识一个实体的名称。
标识符分为未加引号的标识符和反引号标识符。
未加引号的标识符至少包含一个字符。
未加引号的标识符可使用数字、字母和下划线。
反引号标识符由重音符号（`）括起。
反引号标识符可以包含任意字符。
